_comment: Facts about this adapter that its probe response cannot carry: display names, maturity, and the engine versions CI actually restores from. Everything the probe declares (adapter version, engine id, source kinds, pitr) is read from testdata/probe_response.golden instead — never duplicated here. The capabilities generator fails if the source names below do not match the probe exactly, and the integration suite restores from the images listed under verified — the baseline on every run, the rest in the scheduled version matrix and before a release tag — so neither can drift. See docs/capabilities.md and docs/engine-versions.md.
name: PostgreSQL

sources.pgdump: One pg_dump file, custom-format (-Fc) or plain SQL (-Fp), stored plain or gzip-compressed
sources.pgdump_dir: A directory of pg_dump files; source.params.select picks which one is restored — newest by the time each dump records about itself (the default), oldest, or random
sources.pgdump_with_globals: One pg_dump file plus the cluster globals (roles and grants) loaded before it — the dump named by source.params.dump, or picked by source.params.select; either member may be gzip-compressed
sources.barman: A Barman server directory — base/, wals/ and meta/ — restored by placing the cluster and letting PostgreSQL replay the archived WAL
sources.walg: A wal-g filesystem repository — the directory WALG_FILE_PREFIX names, holding basebackups_005 and wal_005 — restored by fetching a base backup and replaying the WAL archive; point-in-time recovery supported, and only the filesystem backend, because a drill's sandbox has no network
sources.timescaledb_dump: One pg_dump file of a TimescaleDB database; the restore is framed with timescaledb_pre_restore()/timescaledb_post_restore()
sources.timescaledb_dump_dir: A directory of them; chosen the way pgdump_dir chooses, framed the same way
sources.timescaledb_dump_with_globals: A directory holding a pg_dumpall --globals-only script and one TimescaleDB dump; the globals load first, then the framed restore
